recipes.name: SOUS VIDE
instructions: For Pork Belly:
Peel and roughly chop ginger, cloves of garlic, and green onions and place into a bowl. - 1 ginger - 2 cloves garlic - 2 green onions
Add soy sauce, mirin, fish sauce, and plain white sugar then whisk thoroughly together. - ½ cup of soy sauce - ½ cup of mirin - ¼ cup fish sauce - ½ cup of plain white sugar
Roll the pork belly up like carpet followed by tying down with butcher twine. - 1 piece of pork belly
Tie every half inch along the pork belly with a surgeon's knot, or whatever knot seems fit. - 1 piece of pork belly

Place the pork belly into a sealed bag with the marinade giving the meat a few turns to fully coat it in the marinade. - 1 piece of pork belly - ½ cup of soy sauce - ½ cup of mirin - ¼ cup fish sauce - ½ cup of plain white sugar
Carefully vacuum seal the bag (be sure to seal it enough for juices to not be sucked into your vacuum.). - 1 piece of pork belly
Roll around a few times to coat the meat. - 1 piece of pork belly
Place the meat into the sous vide with a temperature of 170°F for 6-8 hours. - 1 piece of pork belly
To finish the pork, you can glaze it with the marinade, broil it, or pan fry it. - ½ cup of soy sauce - ½ cup of mirin - ¼ cup fish sauce - ½ cup of plain white sugar
For the Tonkotsu Ramen
https://www.babi.sh/recipes/tonkotsuramen
For Pasteurized Eggs for Edible Cookie Dough:
Place the eggs into the sous vide with a temperature of 135°F for 2 hours. - 4 eggs
After 2 hours, take the eggs out and place into ice cold water - 4 eggs - ice cold water
Use eggs in whatever cookie dough recipe you may have. - 4 eggs
For Porterhouse Steak:

Vacuum seal a 2-inch porterhouse steak with thyme and rosemary, and garlic and place in sous vide at 125°F for 2 hours. - 2 inch thick porterhouse steak - sprig of thyme - sprig of rosemary - 1 clove garlic
After 2 hours, remove the steak from the bag and set the garlic and herbs to the side. - 2 inch thick porterhouse steak
Preheat your cast iron skillet with some oil. You want the cast iron to be as hot as possible.
Salt and pepper the steak thoroughly before placing into the skillet. - salt - black pepper - 2 inch thick porterhouse steak
Blast the steak with as much heat as possible for 90 seconds on each side, or until a beautiful brown crust forms. - 2 inch thick porterhouse steak

After a brown crust has formed, add the herbs and garlic from the vacuum bag along with a generous amount of butter and bacon fat to the pan. - sprig of thyme - sprig of rosemary - 1 clove garlic - butter - bacon fat
Baste the bubbling hot fat on top of the steak until nice and brown. - 2 inch thick porterhouse steak
Once the steak has cooked, take it off the heat and carve it up. - 2 inch thick porterhouse steak
Cut the tenderloin off one side, and the NY Strip off the other end. - 2 inch thick porterhouse steak
Fan them out along the bone and enjoy.
